To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the physicochemical parameters of the aqueous phase (pH and concentration of surfactant) and the organic phase (solvent, concentration of polymer, and concentration of organic solvent) are associated with NP formation.
the NP preparation methods are affected by the physicochemical parameters of the aqueous phase, the organic phase, the solvent, and the solubility of the drug.

the size and size distribution of the NPs are determined by the physicochemical parameters of the aqueous phase (pH and ionic strength), the organic phase (solvent and polymer), and the process (salting-out, emulsion-diffusion, or nanoprecipitation).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods for the preparation and characterization of nanosized particles of biodegradable polymers, and with the development of novel drug delivery systems based on such particles.

the following: (1) to study the physicochemical parameters of the phases used in NP preparation, such as the solubility, the partition coefficient, the diffusion coefficient, the viscosity, and the surface tension, and (2) to relate these parameters to NP formation.
the following questions: (i) Which parameters influence the formation of NP in the salting-out, nanoprecipitation, and emulsification-difusion methods?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physicochemical parameters associated with the aqueous and the organic phases used for NP formation are important in determining the physicochemical characteristics and the size of the NP formed.

the physicochemical parameters associated with the aqueous and oil phases, as well as with the organic solvent and the surfactant, play an important role in NP formation and size control, regardless of the preparation method employed.

the physicochemical parameters of the phases used to prepare NPs are the most important factors for the production of NP, and these factors should be taken into consideration when developing new NP preparation processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salting-out method produced the largest NP, the nanoprecipitation method produced the smallest NP, and the emulsification-difusion method produced NP with intermediate size.

the NP formation is a function of the solubility of the drug in the aqueous and the organic phase, the partition coefficient of the drug between the aqueous and oil phases, the solubility and the partition coefficient of surfactant, and the solubility, partition coefficient, and the molecular weight of cosurfactant.
the physicochemical parameters of the aqueous phase are more relevant for NP formation than those of the organic phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no universal physicochemical parameters associated with NP formation.
the formation of NP by these methods is a function of the physicochemical characteristics of the aqueous/organic phases and the solubility and partition coefficients of the drug.
the physicochemical parameters of the organic and aqueous phases used for NP preparation are important for the formation of NP and can be used as a guide to predict the formation of NP.
